answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, so repeated identities inside a sybil cluster cannot create trusted paths from the honest core. If the cluster has volume vol(S) and few external attestations, its conductance φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S) is low; the probability walks enter it is constrained by that sparse cut, bounding its aggregate voting weight. Nodes named river, forge, and opal gain no extra influence merely by multiplying identities internally.
